ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On December 17, 2019, China's first domestically built aircraft carrier, the "Shandong," was delivered to the navy at a military port in Sanya, Hainan. President Xi Jinping, Chairman of the Central Military Commission, attended the commissioning ceremony. With the advancement of technology, future Chinese aircraft carriers will be equipped with electromagnetic catapults to shorten the takeoff distance of aircraft. As shown in the figure, the total length of the horizontal runway of an aircraft carrier is $l$, and a linear motor is installed in the electromagnetic catapult zone, which can provide a constant traction force of $4.0 \times 10^{4} \, \mathrm{N}$. An aircraft with a mass of $m = 2.0 \times 10^{4} \, \mathrm{kg}$ has a jet engine that can provide a constant thrust of $1.2 \times 10^{5} \, \mathrm{N}$. Assuming that the resistance force on the aircraft during the runway is always 0.2 times the weight of the aircraft, the speed at the end of the runway when taking off from the carrier is $\upsilon = 36 \, \mathrm{m/s}$. The time taken for the aircraft to move in the latter part of the runway is 4 seconds longer than the time taken in the catapult zone. Assuming the aircraft carrier remains stationary and the aircraft can be treated as a point mass with constant mass, the gravitational acceleration is $g = 10 \, \mathrm{m/s}^{2}$.

1. Find the speed of the aircraft as it leaves the electromagnetic catapult zone.
2. Find the length $x$ of the electromagnetic launch zone
3. Find the total length of the runway $l$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the aircraft carrier deck/runway is approximately a horizontal straight runway; the left end is marked with “electromagnetic ejection area” (electromagnetic catapult area), whose length is represented by x; the aircraft first passes through this electromagnetic catapult area, then enters the remaining runway on the right, until the end of the runway, and the total length of the entire runway is l. Then reason: the aircraft mass m=2.0×10^4 kg, g=10 m/s^2, so the weight mg=2.0×10^5 N. The resistance is constantly 0.2 times the weight: f=0.2mg=4.0×10^4 N. In the electromagnetic catapult area, it is subjected to engine thrust 1.2×10^5 N, electromagnetic traction force 4.0×10^4 N, and resistance 4.0×10^4 N, so the resultant force is 1.2×10^5+4.0×10^4-4.0×10^4=1.2×10^5 N, and the acceleration a1=F/m=1.2×10^5/(2.0×10^4)=6 m/s^2. After leaving the electromagnetic catapult area, the electromagnetic traction force disappears, the resultant force is 1.2×10^5-4.0×10^4=8.0×10^4 N, and the acceleration a2=8.0×10^4/(2.0×10^4)=4 m/s^2. Let the time for the aircraft to move in the electromagnetic catapult area be t, then the time for the latter section of motion is t+4. The aircraft starts from rest, and the speed when leaving the electromagnetic catapult area is v1=a1t=6t. The final speed is 36 m/s, therefore 36=v1+a2(t+4)=6t+4(t+4). Solving gives 36=10t+16, t=2 s. Therefore the speed when leaving the electromagnetic catapult area is v1=6×2=12 m/s. The length of the electromagnetic catapult area x=1/2·a1·t^2=1/2×6×2^2=12 m. The time for the latter section is t+4=6 s, and the displacement of the latter section s2=v1(t+4)+1/2·a2·(t+4)^2=12×6+1/2×4×6^2=72+72=144 m. The total runway length l=x+s2=12+144=156 m.
